entries.reason: The transform applies once. I checked the result against all 29 carriers: 6 already in the packet and 23 incoming retag seats. Pass 1: 'The passage says something different.' no longer says how many lines hold the contrary. So it now holds on ENG-017-CR-03 and ENG-019-BV-02, where the contrary is in two places, and on the nine carriers where it runs across a printed line break. On every remaining carrier the passage, by the carrier's own execution, states the contrary of the option. Examples: pp-13 (lines 41-42, Darcy speaking occasionally), pp-20 ('not handsome enough to tempt me'), BB-03 (river 'rising fast'), TM-11 ('a little thing like that', line 63, which I read in the passage), LP-06 (he knew whose jumper it was), ML-10 (he would have refused) and TI-12 (he would not have shown himself). 'Go back and find it.' is a move, and it holds on all 29. Misfiled carriers, checked myself, make genuinely different mistakes. ENG-001-WIW-21: nothing states or denies that he is homesick, which is en-plausible-not-stated. ENG-023-RT-02: Nag's fear is moved in time, and the contrary is only inferred from 'never met a live cobra'. Both are item faults. RT-02 has no entry to go to and belongs with the noEntry time-displacement class. For the same reason the unchanged description ('explicitly denies') is false only on those two misfiles. Pass 2: the sentences are 5 and 5 words, end on full stops, and use British English. The hint sends the child to the passage rather than to what sounds likely, which is the right move for a stated contrary. Meaning is unchanged: only the line count went. One carrier is thin: ENG-028-PR-02 rests on 'Line 7 has her eyes doing the counting', and I could not read that line, because the stream-b passage holding it is not in the agent-review english packets.

resultText.childHint: The passage says something different. Go back and find it.
resultText.description: Chooses an option the passage explicitly denies, rather than one it merely fails to support. Distinguished from a plausible option the passage never states: here the passage states the contrary. Negation-dropped loses a WORD; this loses a CLAIM, and the option may share no wording with the line that refutes it.

entries.reason: All three transforms apply once. Check against the approvalNote: the entry exists because 'structure had NO tag - one-word paragraphs and lists of three were untaggable'. So it was meant to cover structure in general, and the length-only wording was narrower than its own purpose. The widening to 'how the writer has built it' and 'what their shape does' brings the text back in line with that purpose rather than changing it. The new description's examples (a short sentence, a count that grows or shrinks) and its general clause both cover one-word paragraphs and lists of three. Pass 1: ENG-002-pp-07 (twelve, then six, then five) and ENG-006-TM-07 (a second, a third, a fourth, a fifth) are both shapes the question asks about. On both, the carrying option reads content ('counts the guests carefully', 'well organised'), so both the hint and the description hold. 'it' in 'how the writer has built it' points to the part the stem names. That is slightly loose on pp-07 (three numbers), but it is not false. Misfile ENG-007-LP-12, checked myself: its question is about feeling shown through what is held back (indirect characterisation), not the form of a sentence, paragraph or list. Its option names the right surface ('only the old clothes') and denies the effect ('we get nothing else'). That is a different mistake from reading content where the question asks about shape, so here it is an item fault. CROSS-GROUP FLAG: the revised verdicts-B (which I attested in transform-review-BE2) also lists LP-12 as misfiled out of en-inference-literal-lookalike, while this verdict says lookalike is where it belongs. Both cannot be true. LP-12 currently has no entry that fits, and it should go to noEntry rather than be retagged by either group. Pass 2: the sentences are 12 and 7 words, end on '.' and '?', and use British English. The hint names the move (how it is built, then what that does for the reader), and a child can act on it. Note for David/Annie: the entry's text is recorded as Annie's ('approvedByPerson: Annie'). This attests the widened wording as a fix consistent with her approvalNote, under rev-agent-01. It is not her approval of the new text.
